name: Hindustan Media Ventures Ltd
title: Hindustan Media Ventures Ltd - 533217 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Print ad yields drove a 100bp consolidated margin gain to 23% in Q4 on flat volumes, while Radio and OTTplay losses were cut by surrendering six loss-making frequencies and exiting OTTplay; no formal guidance given.

triggers.label: Ad yields up; volumes flat
triggers.quote: the lever for the growth in revenue is primarily yields, volumes have been by and large flat

triggers.quote: those are the frequencies that we've surrendered back to the Government of India

triggers.label: OTTplay discontinued; no residual value
triggers.quote: we've decided to call it quits on OTT play

triggers.label: Radio revenue down on high event base
triggers.quote: The Radio business faced a tough year with revenue declining on a full year basis

red_flags.quote: there are quite a few mark-to-market losses that have impacted us as on 31 st March

summary.headline: HMVL Q4 FY26: consolidated EBITDA up 5% to INR 131 crore on 23% margin despite revenue down 2% to INR 558 crore, driven by Print ad yields.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue was flat for FY26 while EBITDA rose 8% to INR 298 crore, with margin up about 100 bps both for the quarter and the year. Print drove the improvement, with advertising growth led by yield (rate) increases rather than volume. Radio revenue fell on a high events-led base and remained loss-making at operating EBITDA level, and the company surrendered six loss-making radio frequencies. Management is discontinuing the OTTplay digital subscription business, with residual servicing costs expected mainly in FY27. Net cash stays above INR 1,000 crore, but other income fell about INR 50 crore on mark-to-market losses on treasury holdings.

segments.name: Print (operating)
segments.commentary: Q4 operating revenue INR 427 crore (advertising INR 313 crore, up 10%; circulation INR 51 crore, up 4%) with operating EBITDA INR 97 crore at 23% margin. FY26 operating revenue INR 1,500 crore (up 8%), advertising INR 1,148 crore (up 8%), operating EBITDA INR 208 crore at 14% margin.

segments.name: Print English
segments.commentary: Q4 advertising INR 172 crore (up 9%); FY26 advertising INR 644 crore (up 8%). Q4 circulation INR 13 crore (up 13%); FY26 circulation INR 53 crore (down 5%).

segments.name: Print Hindi
segments.commentary: Q4 advertising INR 142 crore (up 12%); FY26 advertising INR 504 crore (up 8%). Circulation virtually flat at INR 38 crore in Q4 and INR 155 crore for FY26.

segments.name: Radio
segments.commentary: Q4 operating revenue INR 43 crore with operating EBITDA of minus INR 7 crore; FY26 revenue INR 140 crore with operating EBITDA of minus INR 22 crore. Revenue declined on high prior-year events base; six loss-making frequencies surrendered to the government.

segments.name: Digital (Shine and Mosaic, continuing operations)
segments.commentary: Q4 operating revenue flat at INR 39 crore with operating EBITDA of minus INR 2 crore. FY26 operating revenue flat at INR 155 crore with operating EBITDA of minus INR 8 crore (about minus 5% margin).

guidance_outlook: Management does not provide formal revenue or earnings guidance.
OTTplay stopped selling new subscriptions from 1 April 2026; existing subscriptions service for one to six months, with a small possible tail to September 2026, and minor losses expected in FY27.
Exit from OTTplay content, ISP and channel partner contracts will involve cash outflows, but management says P&L impact will be marginal.
Management said no further exceptional or discontinued-operation closure losses are expected, though statutory impacts from new labour codes may arise.
Management hopes ad yields are sustainable 'to an extent' and aims to keep deals at or above current levels, while flagging likely competitor reaction.
capex_capacity: Copy share gains in selected markets with a conscious strategy; circulation volumes broadly tracking industry and FY26 copy growth accepted as a trade-off for long-term share.
Radio: surrendered six loss-making frequencies (five plus one earlier) to the government; all remaining frequencies described as profitable.
OTTplay wound down; no residual value expected from brand or distribution after failed partner talks.
Investment in digital businesses to be prioritised, mainly through Digicontent Ltd, with further investment behind core print copies.
Assetvault Ltd (brand AasaanWill) investment of INR 22 crore described as non-cash, paid through AFE (ad space) arrangements.
demand_pricing: Print ad growth was driven by yield (ad rate) increases, with volumes broadly flat in line with industry; management said pricing effort spans both Hindi and English.
Circulation realisation per copy was slightly flat to marginally up; circulation yields broadly flat YoY and revenue growth came mainly from higher copies.
Newsprint costs rising, amplified by a weaker rupee and global supply-chain, trade-policy and geopolitical risks; managed with cost discipline.
Radio faces sector-wide industry pressure and a high events-led prior-year base.
Other operating income in Q4 rose sharply (about INR 32 crore vs about half that a year earlier), attributed to forfeiture of contractual AFE revenue not received within the specified period.

qa_highlights.question: Are ad revenue gains from volumes or pricing, and is it across Hindi and English?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly yield-led pricing, with volumes broadly flat and tracking industry; the pricing effort applies across both Hindi and English, and management is unsure how much is structural.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other operating income rise almost 100% YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: It is due to forfeiture of contractual AFE revenue that counterparties did not pay within the specified period.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the PY Print segment revenue restated by about INR 6 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: OTTplay had advertised in the print newspaper; with OTTplay moved to discontinued operations, the intersegment revenue was eliminated, reducing Print revenue and PBIT by the same amount.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other income fall about INR 50 crore, and why invest INR 22 crore in Assetvault?
qa_highlights.answer: Other income fell on mark-to-market losses on the treasury as yield curves hit record highs (10Y near 7%); management plans to hold to maturity. Assetvault is an AFE investment with no cash outlay and is a marketing-property partnership.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be further exceptional or closure losses from Radio and OTTplay?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no further closure losses are expected; the only likely items are small servicing losses in FY27 and statutory impacts from new labour codes.

qa_highlights.question: Does the Board plan to return cash to shareholders?
qa_highlights.answer: No such plan so far; the Board intends to invest the cash in core print and digital businesses of tomorrow.

risks_watch: Sustainability of ad yield gains given likely competitor response and the stated structural uncertainty.
Newsprint cost inflation from rupee weakness and global supply-chain and trade-policy disruption.
Continued mark-to-market pressure on other income while bond yields stay elevated.
Radio segment remains loss-making at EBITDA level, with sector-wide pressure and the need to hold profitability after frequency surrenders.
Cash outflows from exiting OTTplay contracts and possible statutory charges from new labour codes in FY27.
Quality of other operating income, which includes AFE contractual forfeitures that may not recur.
summary.management_tone: Confident on Print pricing and profitability, but guarded on sustainability of yields and on newsprint costs. Candid and direct about exiting OTTplay and Radio loss-makers, while evasive on forward guidance and on cash return to shareholders.
key_quotes: The fourth quarter of 2025-26 and the full year marked a period of decisive transformation for your Company, one characterised by meaningful improvement in profitability, even as consolidated revenue remained broadly stable on an annual basis.
the lever for the growth in revenue is primarily yields, volumes have been by and large flat, which have tracked the industry.
The simple answer is no. But even if you break down the exceptional items in this year, one of the big items which is sitting is consequent to the new labour codes
we've decided to call it quits on OTT play.

financial_highlights.change: down about INR 50 crore from INR 218 crore in FY25

growth.why: No formal revenue guidance; management says it does not provide it. Q4 revenue fell 2% YoY and FY26 revenue was flat, with EBITDA up 5% in Q4 and 8% for FY26 on yield-led print advertising, and management hopes ad yields are sustainable "to an extent" without quantified support. Capacity changes are exits (six radio frequencies surrendered, OTTplay discontinued), not additions.
